title: REPORT on EU-Syria political relations
part_text: 5. Calls on the Commission and the EEAS to establish a monitoring mechanism to continuously assess progress against these clear benchmarks, and to report to Parliament on a regular basis – at least annually, or whenever there is a significant deterioration on the ground – on the implementation of the EU-Syria Cooperation Agreement, the use of EU funds, progress on the political transition, any risks relating to the misappropriation of assistance, the role of armed groups within state structures and the continued applicability of restrictive measures; underlines that any cooperation should also reach vulnerable communities, without discrimination, and be channelled through reliable partners, subject to strict monitoring and due diligence, ensuring that no funds, resources or benefits are directly or indirectly diverted to, or reach, former regime networks, designated terrorist organisations, including Daesh and other listed terrorist entities, extremist and radicalising movements, including Hizb ut-Tahrir and the Muslim Brotherhood, as well as associated networks or proxies operating on behalf of foreign hostile actors, or any internationally sanctioned individuals or entities; calls for the immediate suspension of EU funding, without any further delay, in the event of any breach of these safeguards;
